land.text: 'the Mutsu and Dewa Province' north of the Sendai plain: the Kiyohara lands held under the imperial governor of Mutsu since the Former Nine Years' War

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws nothing here before 1094; the Heian dossier gives the land to the court 1062-1086 (confidence 2) and as a vassal tint from 1087.

land.text: the whole realm: 'Yoritomo entered Hiraizumi' on 3 October 1189

successors.note: Cliopatria adds the land to the Kamakura shogunate in 1192; the conquest was October 1189.

capitals.name: Hiraizumi
capitals.note: At the peak of their rule they 'created a capital city, Hiraizumi'; Chūson-ji 'founded in 1095'. The page gives no capital field.

correction.text: the realm as Cliopatria draws it from 1094, 'the Mutsu and Dewa Province' ruled from Hiraizumi, from 1087

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: infobox founding 1087 ('in 1087, when he won the victory in the Gosannen War'); Cliopatria begins the row in 1094. The lead's span '1094–1104' is unexplained on the page.

44,949 km2: northern Tōhoku from about 38.7 N to the Tsugaru strait. The page says the clan 'ruled the Mutsu and Dewa Province for over a century', provinces that reach south to the Sendai plain and Shōnai where Cliopatria keeps Heian Japan; the southern limit is unverified: page budget. No infobox area.

correction.text: unchanged; holds 1188 to October 1189, when Yasuhira 'fled Hiraizumi leaving it afire'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria runs the row to 1191; Hiraizumi fell on 2-3 October 1189 and Yasuhira was killed on 14 October. The 1188 break is unexplained (identical area).

region.text: 'the Mutsu and Dewa Province' ruled from Hiraizumi

ledger.note: 1087: Fujiwara no Kiyohira founds the Hiraizumi realm after the Gosannen War. Kiyohira 'became independent and established themselves in Hiraizumi ... in 1087, when he won the victory in the Gosannen War'; they 'succeeded the semi-independent Emishi families of the 11th century' and 'were able to keep their independence vis-à-vis Kyoto'.

region.text: Hiraizumi and the realm, against which '284,000 cavalrymen' set out

ledger.note: 1189: Yoritomo's Ōshū campaign. 'After Yoshitsune was assassinated in April 1189' at Yasuhira's hands, his head reached Kamakura 'by July'; on 1 September 1189 Yoritomo set out against Hiraizumi with '284,000 cavalrymen'; Yasuhira 'prepared himself an army of 170,000 cavalrymen'.
1189: Hiraizumi falls. On 2 October Yasuhira 'fled Hiraizumi leaving it afire' and 'Yoritomo entered Hiraizumi the next day'; Yasuhira was 'found and killed in Nienosaku, Hinai' on 14 October.
1189: the realm annexed by Kamakura. 'The Battle of Ōshū resulted in the destruction of the Northern Fujiwara clan', which led to 'the establishment of the Kamakura shogunate'.

region.text: the whole realm, to the Kamakura shogunate

ledger.note: 1189: the Northern Fujiwara destroyed; Ōshū passes to Yoritomo. Infobox dissolution 1189.

wars.name: Gosannen War
wars.outcome: 'Military stalemate'; 'In the end, Iehira and Narihira were killed'; Fujiwara no Kiyohira, who 'helped' Yoshiie, emerged as lord of the former Kiyohara lands and founded the Hiraizumi realm (1087, Northern Fujiwara page).
wars.note: Dates '1083–1089 (disputed)'; Minamoto no Yoshiie 'became Governor of Mutsu province in 1083'; 'the siege of Kanezawa, 1086–1089'. The war that made the state; it is listed here though it predates the founding. The war ran 1083-1089 (disputed); years clipped to the state's life from its 1087 founding (reviewer jk-01-a).

wars.name: Battle of Ōshū
wars.outcome: 'The Battle of Ōshū resulted in the destruction of the Northern Fujiwara clan'; Hiraizumi burned 2 October 1189, Yasuhira killed 14 October.

certainty.note: The southern limit against the court's provinces of Mutsu and Dewa is administrative, not a border; the northern limit (Tsugaru, Ezo trade) is not on the pages.

sources.title: Northern Fujiwara
sources.note: Identity, 1087, Hiraizumi, Mutsu and Dewa, the 1189 campaign with dates; no area, no reign years.

notes: Cliopatria 1094-1191 against the page's 1087-1189: a new keyframe 1087-1093 and the last shape cut to October 1189. The relation to the Kyoto court is unsettled: the page says they 'were able to keep their independence vis-à-vis Kyoto' and never mentions the court titles (Chinjufu-shōgun, governor of Mutsu) or the gold and horse tribute other accounts give, so the Heian and Kamakura dossiers draw a vassal tint at confidence 1. Rulers: the page names Kiyohira, Motohira, Hidehira and Yasuhira without reign years, so no ruler strip. The Abe (to 1062) and Kiyohara (1062-1087) regional powers that preceded them have no Cliopatria row; the Heian dossier treats their land as an Emishi vassal tint (c. 850-1051) and as direct court land (1062-1086); a gap-filler may prefer dossiers of type state for them. The Gosannen page gives nothing on Kiyohira's succession or the move to Hiraizumi; Yoshitsune's flight to Hiraizumi (1187) is undated on the Northern Fujiwara page.
